#1535. 'It's a travesty and not what they were promised': Glazers' anger at Sir Jim Ratcliffe's reign revealed - and why Man United have become debt-loaded inconvenience for absentee landlords as they splash cash on true loves

Published: 13:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EDT, 29 October 2026

From a safe distance in Florida, out of the line of fire, the Glazer family are happy for others to let it be known they are disenchanted with how they believe the British businessman who paid them £1.5billion for a minority share in Manchester United has mismanaged the club.

‘It’s a travesty and not what they expected or were promised,’ a source with a social connection to the family tells Daily Mail Sport of Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s disastrous custodianship. ‘They have never run the club this way.’

Another source told the US broadcaster ESPN this week that the Glazers believe Ratcliffe ‘couldn't have masterminded a worse situation’. His ‘downgrading in all departments’ at Old Trafford was ‘the opposite of what he said his strategy is’.

It would be unwise to characterise this Glazer concern as sentiment. Cash is the motivating factor, just as always. United are two points off the bottom of the Premier League ahead of Saturday’s trip to Chelsea and the $6bn (£4.5bn) valuation which the Glazers put on the club when seeking a buyer, four years ago, is looking more unrealistic than ever.

The Glazers control any sale. A clause in their deal with Ratcliffe, completed in 2024, lets them force him out of his 28 per cent stake – and out of the entire landscape – if they sell the club to a third party, without him having any say, unless he can match that offer and buy the entire club himself. Which is highly improbable.

Whatever displeasure they might feel, they can’t buy back Ratcliffe’s piece of the United pie. But from next February, Ratcliffe will be powerless to stop them selling the entire club for a price lower than the $33 (£25) a share he paid for his chunk. As of Thursday, the United share price was just $20.77 (£15.60).

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (right) with Man United co-chairman Avram Glazer, who is rarely seen at Old Trafford and has never given a meaningful interview about the club he owns

United fans make clear their disgust at the way the club is being run by the Glazers and Ineos

Ratcliffe’s Ineos are cutting their losses in football. They put their Swiss club FC Lausanne-Sport up for sale this week and have slashed the asking price for their French club Nice.

They could sell their chunk of United to someone else if at least two of Ineos’ three shareholders – Ratcliffe and company co-founders Andrew Currie and John Reece – agree to it. The Glazers, for their part, may want to see United’s new stadium built, hiking up the value, before selling. That might not be completed until 2035.

More than ever, the Glazers are absentee landlords. A family with far bigger fish to fry than their struggling Premier League asset where fans sing against them. A family who have been extremely active elsewhere while Old Trafford burns.

In February, Avram Glazer, one of the six siblings, bid $1.32bn (£1bn) for the Royal Challengers Bengaluru franchise in cricket's Indian Premier League, where the enormous market and broadcasting rights deals have seen stratospheric returns on investment. Only as the franchise’s valuation approached a prohibitive $2bn (£1.5bn) did Glazer withdraw. His bid for the Rajasthan Royals was also retracted.

And then there is the love of the Glazers’ lives – their Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFL franchise – where their active involvement provides a striking contrast to their loveless 21-year ownership of United.

While the family have managed to go all these years without a single meaningful UK media interview about United – Avram Glazer hastily climbed into his Aston Martin and drove off when doorstepped by a Sky TV reporter in Florida, five years ago – a recent Amazon series about the Buccaneers provided a rare glimpse into the world of these billionaires.

Like so many such series, Raise the Flags is sanitised and glossy, with Ed Glazer, another of the siblings, one of its executive producers. But it paints a revealing picture of how the NFL-mad Glazers tried and failed for years to buy into the sport, which was intrinsic to the siblings’ childhoods, until the death of Bucs owner Hugh Culverhouse finally gave Malcolm Glazer, their father, his chance in 1995.

They were seen as saviours at a franchise which was ridiculed for always losing and at risk of relocation to Baltimore, Maryland, 1,000 miles away. They transformed it, appointing rookie coach Tony Dungy and even changing the colours from garish neon orange to red and pewter grey.

Joel Glazer, who last visited Old Trafford in 2019, becomes emotional as he tells filmmakers about the team’s legendary win under Dungy, against the San Francisco 49ers in 1997, which set them on the way from hapless also-rans to two-time Super Bowl winners.

Manchester United co-owner Joel Glazer celebrates Super Bowl glory in 2021 when his beloved Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Kansas City Chiefs

The Bucs, not United, is what gets the Glazers out of bed. It’s what they spend their own money on – and that will include a $1bn (£750m) rebuild of the team’s Raymond James stadium

‘You know, you felt we’d turned the corner,’ he says, his voice breaking. There is an authenticity about this.

The Bucs, not Manchester United, is what gets these brothers out of bed in the morning. It’s what they spend their own money on – and that will include a $1bn (£750m) rebuild of the team’s Raymond James stadium – the ‘RayJay’ – which is old, dated and lacks the roof required for Tampa to host a lucrative Super Bowl. Within two months, the Glazers and the Bucs will outline plans for the overhaul, to conform with a deadline for a lease extension on the ground.

United have their own stadium plans, of course. But the Glazers didn’t even attend the event at Old Trafford in March 2025, at which architect Sir Norman Foster’s proposals, with their distinctive, canopy-like roof, were presented.

While United are a globally recognised brand and the Bucs are a franchise little known beyond the US, there is no doubt which of these two Glazer sports businesses holds most financial value.

The wild expectation that United would fetch $6bn was born of the values of NFL franchises such as Washington Commanders, on the market for $8bn (£6bn) at the time they put United up for sale. The Commanders were eventually sold for $6.05bn (£4.45bn) to a consortium led by Josh Harris, who also has a big chunk of Crystal Palace. There was no offer anywhere in that vicinity for United.

In part, NFL teams have become so valuable because of a US tax break which allows owners to claim tax deductions on things their teams own or pay for and shrink the amount of profit they pay tax on. It means billionaire owners like the Glazers can end up paying a lower percentage of their income in tax than the workers who keep the stadium running.

In the NFL, the Seattle Seahawks were sold in early September for $9.6bn (£7.2bn), a world record for a sports franchise that lasted just a few days until basketball’s LA Lakers changed hands for $12.5bn (£9.3bn) – more than double United’s industry valuation.

With a precious NFL asset to protect and build, United, whose football operations have been ceded to Ratcliffe, are a minor consideration.

Joel and Avram Glazer are often seen in and around the Bucs - but are rarely spotted at Old Trafford

Former Bucs head coach Tony Dungy was once under pressure like Michael Carrick is now but the Glazers stood by their man - and felt the benefits

Though the Amazon series is PR-friendly and soft focus, it offers an intriguing insight into what active Glazer involvement can look like. When the first draft under their ownership takes place, some of the brothers are in the Buccaneers ‘War Room’ witnessing the squad being built.

When Coach Dungy struggles with no wins in five in his second season and faces a critique like the one Michael Carrick is now encountering, the Glazers call him in for lunch. Rather than tell him he is fired – as he expects – they talk things over for four hours and put him at ease. Dungy’s testimony corroborates the notion that they helped him.

Joel Glazer was often seen as a meddling man of interference at United, prior to Ratcliffe moving in. He would ask for higher fees and drive harder deals when executive chairman Ed Woodward or others were trying to negotiate.

The family never wanted an Amazon documentary about United and only now, under Ratcliffe, has the streaming business got into the corridors of the club. The Glazers’ key United manoeuvres, still very much going on, take place behind closed doors.

The evidence of the past year points to them continuing to use the club as collateral to secure huge loans which helps them invest in other parts of their business empire, according to a study by the respected football finance expert Paul Quinn, popularly known as ‘The Esk’.

Quinn highlights a UK Companies House filing from February, ‘Charge 0018’, through which United took out a Bank of America mortgage against land near Old Trafford, and other club assets, to potentially generate cash for the Glazers. The loan arrangement, taking United’s maximum credit facility up to £400m, came a few weeks before Avram Glazer submitted his huge bids for an IPL franchise.

There is no evidence that the new borrowing secured by Charge 0018 funded an IPL bid, or that Manchester United’s money was used to finance one.

More than ever, it is the Glazers’ own elusive cash that the club need. That new £2billion stadium won’t build itself and though there are plenty of ways of finding the money, the Financial Times has pointed out while listing them that they will ‘not come cheap’.

More than ever, it is the Glazers’ own elusive cash that Manchester United need. That new £2billion stadium won’t build itself

Carrick will be fighting for his future when his United team take on Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday

Tapping into the bond market as Barcelona did to finance their $1.5bn upgrade of Camp Nou would leave the club more exposed to global interest rates. Private equity funds would want a major pay-back when the stadium is built, limiting United’s capacity to earn from the new structure.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers play Atlanta Falcons at the RayJay on Sunday and there can be no doubt that some of the Glazer brothers will be there. Bryan, Joel and Avram were in the team locker room after last weekend’s win at the Carolina Panthers, by all accounts smiling and clapping as coach Todd Bowles spoke.

They hardly ever watch United these days and will certainly not be at Stamford Bridge to see Carrick fighting for his future. Their Premier League asset is an inconvenience, loaded down with debt payments, running up losses for the past seven years and, on Ratcliffe’s watch, reduced to selling clumps of Old Trafford turf for £125.

Where are the Glazers? More than 4,000 miles away from all that.

#1534. Como: big blow for Moise Kean

Bad news for Cesc Fàbregas and Como. Already hampered by physical problems in recent weeks, Moise Kean will have to wait before returning to the field. The Italian international striker underwent a medical procedure in Barcelona to treat a shin injury, his club announced in an official statement. “ Como 1907 announces that Moise Kean was treated at the Cugat Institute in Barcelona for a recent tibia injury. The treatment was a success. The convalescence time is estimated at approximately five weeks and will be assessed daily depending on the clinical evolution. », Specifies the Lombard formation. An additional absence which should postpone his return to December and which constitutes a real blow for Como, engaged on several tables this season.

Recruited this summer from Fiorentina for nearly 40 million euros, Moise Kean arrived with the ambition of reaching a new milestone under the orders of Cesc Fàbregas. But his physical problems complicate his integration and now deprive Como of an important offensive solution for its next Serie A and Champions League matches. This unavailability should also prevent the former Juventus player from joining Roberto Mancini’s Italian selection at the next international gathering. In his absence, Anastasios Douvikas should benefit from more playing time at the forefront of the attack.

#1533. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Sep 8: Club Brugge vs Aston VillaOct 14: Aston Villa vs Fenerbahçe Oct 21: Aston Villa vs Viking Nov 3: Barcelona vs Aston VillaNov 24: Galatasaray vs Aston Villa Dec 8: Aston Villa vs Paris St-Germain Jan 19: Aston Villa vs Borussia DortmundJan 27: Slavia Praha vs Aston Villa

Quite the evening, last time out at the Jan Breydel Stadium 💫 pic.twitter.com/NogGLLSMFU

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1532. Tuttosport: Milan considering return attempt with Athekame with talks expected in January

AC Milan are beginning to explore the possibility of an early return for Zachary Athekame, after his start to life in France.

When they signed Athekame in the summer of 2025, Milan were aware that he was a player for the future. Nevertheless, he was still given occasional minutes last season and he could’ve been given more.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He also could’ve stayed this season; in hindsight, things are viewed differently. Yet, there would be an argument that he’d have provided some quality depth in a position of makeshift options.

According to Tuttosport this morning, via MilanPress, the Rossoneri would be keen to bring Athekame back from his loan spell in France early for several reasons. Firstly, the Swiss has reached a new level in France this season, so his return would be a permanent one.

Then, the injury issues mean that the squad is weak at full-back. So, with Ruben Amorim looking to a four-back system more frequently, he could help a lot.

It won’t be as easy as just recalling him, though. Lyon still need to be convinced and there was no agreement for his return before the summer. With this, the French club have already hinted that a fee would be required for an early return.

Talks are expected to take place in January and with Paulo Fonseca leaving the club, Athekame’s perspective on things could change. We shall have to see.

#1531. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1530. FC Barcelona: Jules Koundé forfeits the Clasico

It was in the air, it is now official: Jules Koundé will not play the Clasico against Real Madrid, scheduled for this Sunday at 9 p.m., on behalf of the 10th day of La Liga. Hit in the left ankle during FC Barcelona’s victory against Betis (5-2) last weekend, the French defender did not recover in time from his sprain.

His absence was confirmed this Saturday by Hansi Flick at a press conference: “Jules Koundé will not be available tomorrow, we do not want to take any risks with him“, explained the German coach. Barça will also have to deal without Eric Garcia and Dani Olmo. To compensate for the absence of Koundé, Flick could line up the same defense as during the defeat against PSG (4-2) in the Champions League.

#1529. Juventus and Napoli meet level on 14 points as Allegri ban and Lobotka injury bite

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday with both sides on 14 points and both short of key figures. Spalletti is missing seven players, while Napoli lose their suspended coach and their midfield organiser Lobotka.

Juventus and Napoli go into Sunday’s Serie A Matchday 10 meeting at the Allianz Stadium level on points. Both benches will look different. Napoli will be without their head coach, with assistant Landucci on the bench. Spalletti is still missing seven players.

Allegri was sent off in Napoli’s 3-3 home draw with Roma. Serie A’s sporting judge then punished him for disrespectful remarks to the match officials. The ban covered the trip to Monza on 28 October and now the visit to Juventus. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri dropped it, saying he feared the ban could rise to four matches. The suspension is now final.

Napoli also lost Lobotka at Monza. He was stretchered off just after the 15th minute following a challenge with Mangas. The club’s medical update found damage to the tibiofibular syndesmosis in his left ankle, without instability. He also has a low-grade injury to the anterior talofibular ligament. He has started rehabilitation, with Napoli aiming for a return against Fiorentina in the Coppa Italia on 16 December. Badiashile and Neres are also injured.

The Juventus list is longer. Yildiz is expected back in early December after a foot operation, Sky Sport Italia reported. Thuram, who had knee surgery, is due back in early 2027. Locatelli is out until 2027 after a lateral meniscus operation. Grabara, with a right-knee ACL injury, is effectively out for the season.

Nico González (right soleus), Çelik (left hamstring) and Conceição (shoulder dislocation) are all expected back after the international break. There is one return. Young forward Ekhator is available again.

Juventus arrive after an uneven run. Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on 18 October. Spalletti’s side then won at Lecce on 25 October, with goals from McKennie and Douglas Luiz. Genoa won the next game through first-half goals from Ehizibue and Baldanzi. Koopmeiners hit the crossbar in stoppage time.

After the Genoa defeat, chief executive Carnevali held a long meeting with the squad. He told them to change course straight away, especially in their mentality. Spalletti then announced the squad would stay together from Friday evening until the Napoli game. The club wants the response to come from the players on the pitch rather than from a change of coach. John Elkann still backs Spalletti, and the coach has no intention of giving up, according to Tuttosport.

🗣️ "There’s only one way to win games: you have to want it more than your opponents"

The Bianconeri host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Serie A Matchday 10, and coach Luciano Spalletti previewed the action ⤵️

🗞️ https://t.co/8lyakgqdxW#JuveNapoli pic.twitter.com/KGApOET8on

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 31, 2026

The fixture also brings Spalletti back against Napoli, the club he won the title with. The last meeting, in January 2026 at the Allianz Stadium, ended 3-0 to Juventus. Jonathan David, Kenan Yildiz and Filip Kostić scored. A win on Sunday would lift Juventus clear of a direct rival. Spalletti’s pre-match press conference is set for Saturday 31 October at 17:00, the day before kick-off.

With talk of Krösche joining Milan, there has always been suggestions that his number two could arrive as well. Indeed, the German’s relationship and CV with Hardung speak for themselves, with the pair reimagining the Eintracht Frankfurt model.

The duo are credited almost completely with the work done across recent years and the Rossoneri have always had an interest in hiring both. Yet, it seemed that it would be impossible recently, thanks to Hardung moving into Krösche’s old role. But that may not be the case.

According to Matteo Moretto, the German could still head to Italy – with Krösche – despite his new role with Frankfurt, as MilanNews relays from his appearance on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel.

“Despite Milan’s denials, Krosche will be the club’s new Head of Football. I also want to clarify the possible role of Timmo Hardung, sporting director of Eintracht Frankfurt. Timmo Hardung is Krosche’s right-hand man, with whom he has been working for some time.

“The Frankfurt club has confirmed him within the structure, but it is not 100% certain that he will remain in Germany. Milan is sticking with him, Krosche holds him in high regard, and it cannot be ruled out that Milan could also make an attempt for him in the coming weeks.

“Hardung has several offers – there are several clubs that hold him in high regard even in Germany such as Nuremberg and Hannover – but also keep an eye out for the Milan option, which cannot be completely ruled out at this moment.

“Krösche will have to fit into a structure that is already tested, the one built and designed by Gerry Cardinale, however, I don’t rule out that in the coming months, if the opportunity arises, perhaps Milan could also try for Hardung.

“Krösche has great respect for Hardung and considers him extremely well-prepared for his role.”

If Gerry Cardinale could bring both to Casa Milan, it would be a huge statement from him. It would also say a lot about the future of the project.

#1527. Spalletti calls job question provocative and vows no step back before Napoli

Luciano Spalletti struck a defiant tone on the eve of Juventus-Napoli, a game seen as a must-win. He also backed the club's response to the defeat at Genoa, including a squad retreat.

Spalletti made his stance clear on the eve of Juventus-Napoli. Anyone expecting him to retreat even slightly, he warned, should expect something different.

Sunday’s game is at the Allianz Stadium. Spalletti said the side want to win back the respect that has been taken from them. Several outlets say his job is on the line.

The build-up has been shaped by the club’s response to the defeat at Genoa. Ehizibue scored in the 12th minute and Baldanzi in the 28th. After a long meeting between chief executive Giovanni Carnevali and the squad, Spalletti announced a retreat. The team would stay at the Continassa from Friday evening until the Napoli game.

Spalletti called Carnevali’s address perfect and said he had hit the right notes. He has never been keen on training-camp retreats. In these circumstances, though, he said one could help the group become more compact again.

The coach also played down any need for public backing. He needs no reassurance from the club, only a reaction from the team, Eurosport reported. He added that he is not asking his players for anything beyond their capabilities.

After nine rounds, this season’s tally trails the 15 Juventus had at the same stage last season and the 17 under Motta in 2024/25. It is above the 13 under Allegri in 2022/23, according to Tuttosport.

Recent form has been uneven. The last five league results were a 2-0 home win over Atalanta, a 1-1 draw at Cagliari and a 3-0 home defeat by Lazio. A 2-0 win at Lecce and the loss at Genoa complete the run. Two of those five games ended in defeat, and Juventus failed to score in both.

Napoli arrive without their coach. The Serie A sporting judge banned Massimiliano Allegri for two matches over disrespectful remarks to the officials in the 3-3 draw with Roma. The ban covers the Monza and Juventus games.

⏰ Alle 17:00 la conferenza stampa di mister Luciano Spalletti alla vigilia di #JuveNapoli 🎙️

Guardala in diretta su Juventus Play ⚪️⚫️📺 https://t.co/yLSmeRGwZE pic.twitter.com/y0zkMRM6cs

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) October 31, 2026

Spalletti also offered a hint on selection. He said Edon Zhegrova and Jeremie Boga would come on in the second half even if they did not start.

There is little time to recover whatever the result. Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League on Thursday 5 November at 21:00.

#1526. Liverpool Confidential: Inside Harvey Elliott's difficult start to life in Valencia, why experts think move is doomed despite efforts off the pitch, the loanee who IS thriving in Spain and club's stance on making Ronald Araujo deal permanent

Published: 13:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 13:05 EDT, 29 October 2026

Harvey Elliott is working hard to right the wrongs of his first few months at Valencia as another loan away from Liverpool threatens to become a 'significant disappointment' due to concerns over his form, fitness and discipline.

The English midfielder is on loan at the Estadio Mestalla after a rotten year at Aston Villa but he has struggled for game time under two different managers, making just six substitute appearances so far.

And last weekend he suffered the ignominy of being sent off just 19 minutes after coming off the bench at home to Villarreal, who then scored a 90th-minute winner seconds later to leave Valencia second-bottom after 10 games.

Liverpool staff are in constant contact with all their loanees and their clubs to check on players' progress and the last word back from Valencia was that Elliott, 23, is putting in quality work off the pitch to improve physically.

But as Julian Burgos, a Valencia expert, tells Liverpool Confidential: ‘At the moment, I don’t think he has adapted… he has been a significant disappointment, especially considering he arrived with the pedigree of coming from Liverpool.

‘It is true that he has been putting in the work over the last few weeks, and he appears to be in better physical shape.

Harvey Elliott is on loan at Valencia but 'has been a significant disappointment' says Julian Burgos, a Valencia expert

Elliott was sent off against Villarreal at the weekend despite coming on as a substitute

‘Honestly, if the option to terminate the loan arises, Valencia will likely pursue it. With a new sporting director and manager – compounded by the team’s poor form – it seems they will look to undo many of the moves made by the previous sporting director, the Scotsman Ron Gourlay.'

Valencia sacked their previous coach, Carlos Corberan, in mid-September after they picked up just one point in their opening five matches of the season.

‘They need to free up space within the salary cap to make changes to the squad,' Burgos adds, 'so they will likely take any opportunity to cut ties with players brought in under the previous regime.’

Last year, the midfielder was stuck at Aston Villa. Clearly not fancied by their manager Unai Emery, the club prevented him from playing the 10 games that would have meant the deal becoming permanent for £35million, which seemed a foregone conclusion when he joined.

As Elliott featured for Liverpool at the start of last season – a five-minute cameo off the bench in their second game of the campaign – he could not head out on another loan because of a FIFA ruling that states players can only represent two clubs on the pitch in one season.

There is no option or obligation to make his deal permanent at Valencia, whose new manager is Javier Aguirre, whom England fans may remember for his touchline antics with Mexico at the World Cup. Aguirre will give Elliott time to turn his fortunes around. There is an understanding he needed to build fitness after barely playing last year.

The club have appealed last week's red card – for two yellows – and Elliott is said to have apologised to team-mates.

Elliott had a miserable time at Aston Villa last season when he hardly featured for the club

…but it’s not all worrying news in Valencia!

Now let’s head across the city to fellow La Liga club Levante, where one Liverpool loanee is thriving.

Centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe has been touted as having the potential to be ‘one of the best in the world in his position’.

Burgos adds: ‘Since his debut against Sevilla four matches ago, he has established himself as a starter for the manager Luis Castro, who asserted that he possesses the qualities to become one of the best players in the world in his position.

‘Against Sevilla, he recovered from an early mistake to score the equalising goal in stoppage time, and he has been a fixture in the side ever since. At 18, he has an impressive physique, remarkable coordination for his height, and the makings of a great footballer – both for the present and, even more so, for the future.’

Ndukwe could not stay at Liverpool this season due to a work permit issue. Apparently he now has the required points to return to Anfield and a recall clause is included in the deal.

But it might be better to keep Ndukwe there, where he is playing every week, and bleed him into the first-team squad next year.

Liverpool centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe has shone at Levante this season and is now a regular starter for his manager Luis Castro

Ndukwe could not stay at Liverpool this season due to a work permit issue. He now has the required points to return to Anfield

The story of the week at Liverpool has been Ronald Araujo after his man-of-the-match performance against Brighton. The Uruguayan’s status as a cult hero continues to grow and grow.

But are fans naive to fall in love with a loan player? Will Liverpool make the temporary move permanent? And can they do it for less than the clause of £47m?

Last week, I said I’d answer fans’ questions every week in this column and the answers to the Araujo inquiries are…

Absolutely, fans are right to fall in love with him! Liverpool are open to making the move permanent if this form continues, for sure – otherwise why would they insert the option to do so in the deal? People may point to the fact Liverpool would not usually sign a 28-year-old (Araujo turns 28 in March) but look at Virgil van Dijk, still going strong at 35.

And yes, they will be able to negotiate the fee down from the pre-agreed figure with Barcelona.

Ronald Araujo has been sensational for his manager Andoni Iraola this season

Lots of talk about Trent Alexander-Arnold this week given he has fallen out of favour with new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho. It has led many to debate whether Liverpool should re-sign him but Confidential is told Alexander-Arnold remains happy in the Spanish capital.

Regardless, would it be a wise move? Financially, no. Does the team lack his creativity from right back? Yes. Would the fans welcome him back with open arms? No… but stranger things have happened.

Trent Alexander-Arnold has fallen out of favour at Real - but a return to Anfield looks unlikely

Fans of French club Lens have been banned from buying tickets for their team’s Champions League trip to Anfield.

Lens, who finished second in Ligue 1 last year under now Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage, come to Liverpool in the new year. But they will do so – as it stands – without supporters after UEFA banned them from selling away tickets following events in Belgium last week.

In Lens' loss at Bruges, fans were punished for lighting and throwing pyrotechnics – which injured disabled supporters.

The club banned its own fans from buying tickets for this week’s trip to rivals Lille and said in a statement: ‘This situation goes far beyond the realm of the displays that sometimes accompany popular expression in the stands. A red line has been crossed. This line was not implicit.’

Anfield also had an empty away end last year when Galatasaray came to town in the last 16, a match which the Reds won 4-0.

Big Mama’s best night… no thanks to dud water bottle

An important night for Giorgi Mamardashvili against Chelsea on Wednesday.

The big Georgian has had mixed reviews since his arrival from Valencia, with some indifferent performances.

But this was perhaps his best performance yet – not just for his fine penalty save, but some other notable stops as both he and Mike Penders kept the scores level.

Liverpool’s No 2 can poke fun, though, at whoever provided the notes for his water bottle ahead of the shootout. None of the instructions were correct and Mamardashvili was left diving the wrong way several times.

Giorgi Mamardashvili celebrates his side's victory over Chelsea with his team-mate Kostas Tsimikas. It was the goalkeeper's finest performance in a Liverpool shirt

Sunday’s clash with Arsenal is the biggest game so far in the Andoni Iraola era for one reason: it sets the tone for the rest of the season. Lose and Liverpool are nine points behind the champions. Win, though, and it’s only three – with confidence they can beat anyone.

Dominik Szoboszlai is pushing to return but here is a question for you to ponder to finish this week’s column: does last year’s player of the year get back in Iraola’s best XI?
